items.statement: Nurses describing a shift that ran at least 10 percent below planned hours report at least one missed care activity more often than nurses describing a shift at or above plan, and the difference remains after adjustment for the unit's acuity on that day.
items.rationale: Need is high because both management and the union want the answer; novelty is moderate because the conflict over acuity (c2 against c3) is unresolved; linkage to scheduling records is already possible.
items.risks: Nonresponse on night shifts; acuity scores entered inconsistently; small cells on some units.

items.statement: Licensed practical nurses report different missed activities from registered nurses, with more missed teaching and discharge preparation on units with more licensed practical nurses.
items.rationale: Skill mix was linked to missed teaching and discharge preparation in the retrieved multi-hospital survey.
items.risks: Role-specific item meaning without a validated instrument.

items.statement: Most missed care is concentrated on night shifts.
items.rationale: Night shifts showed a steeper increase with shortfall in the linkage study.
items.risks: Different activities are expected at night, so counts are not comparable across shifts.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected because it answers the shared management and union question.
